To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Turkey’s membership in the EU will bring about the greatest benefits to the Turkish economy.
Turkey would gain more from the removal of tariffs than the removal of NTB and that Turkey’s gains from EU membership would be more substantial than from GAFTA membership.

the welfare gains stemming from Turkey’s membership in the EU are considerably larger than the gains from GAFTA, that the welfare gains resulting from the removal of non-tariffs are greater than the welfare gains stemming the elimination of tariffs, and that the removal of non- tariff barriers is more likely to occur in the context of EU membership than GAFTA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of Turkey’s accession to the EU and GAFTA on the Turkish economy and the world economy.
the potential impact of the EU and the GAFTA on Turkey.
the impact of Turkish membership in the EU and the GAFTA on Turkey’s trade flows and welfare.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Turkish membership in GAFTA would not be a viable alternative to EU membership.
Turkish accession to the EU would be the most beneficial alternative for Turkey.
Turkey should pursue EU membership.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Turkey would gain more from EU membership in terms of trade, income, and welfare.
Turkey would gain from EU membership, but the welfare gain from GAFTA membership is relatively limited, especially when the NTBs are not taken into account.
the removal of NTB barriers in the agricultural sector is more important than the elimination of tariffs in the food and agricultural sector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the removal of NTB’s would be a key factor in Turkey’s economic development.
Turkey’s accession to the EU is a much better option for the Turkish economy than joining GAFTA.
Turkey should continue to pursue membership in the EU.
